findings.title: The SendGrid client used by the cancellation cron is never authenticated
findings.body: The handler only calls `sgMail.setApiKey`, which configures the mail service's internal client, not the separately imported `@sendgrid/client` instance used by `client.request` here. Consequently the new scheduled-send cancellation request can be rejected as unauthorized; the outer catch logs the error and leaves the reminder unmodified, so the SendGrid email remains queued and is sent. Configure this `client` with `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` before making requests.

findings.title: A cancellation shortly before send time is not processed before the email is delivered
findings.body: Booking cancellation only marks an email reminder as cancelled, while this job performs the actual SendGrid cancellation on a 15-minute cadence. If the previous cron run has already occurred and a user cancels a booking whose reminder is due before the next run (for example, a reminder due in five minutes), SendGrid will send it before this query executes. The next run deletes the now-past database record without ever preventing the delivery. Imminent reminders need synchronous cancellation or a scheduling/worker design that guarantees cancellation before `sendAt`.

findings.title: Rescheduling bypasses the deferred cancellation mechanism and recreates the SendGrid cancellation-cap failure
findings.body: The reschedule path passes `immediateDelete: true`, causing `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` to POST `status: cancel` to SendGrid immediately and return without setting `WorkflowReminder.cancelled`. Therefore these records are never handled or retried by the cron job. SendGrid retains each such far-future cancellation until its scheduled date; after enough reschedules the provider's pending-cancellation limit is reached, cancellation failures are swallowed, and old reminders are sent. Reschedules should persist a retryable cancelled state and use the bounded cron cancellation path (with separate handling for imminent sends).

findings.title: Paid booking cancellations return before any workflow reminder is cancelled
findings.body: For a paid booking this branch refunds the payment, changes the booking to `REJECTED`, and returns at line 464. The workflow-reminder cancellation loop that marks email reminders cancelled and removes SMS reminders is below this return at lines 484-493, so it is never reached. Scheduled workflow emails for paid bookings remain active and will still be delivered after cancellation. Move reminder and scheduled-job cancellation before the paid-booking early return or execute it in that branch.

findings.title: Reminder cancellation state updates are fire-and-forget
findings.body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async, but the calls inside these `forEach` loops are neither awaited nor included in the later `Promise.all`. The cancellation endpoint can report success before the `cancelled` marker is persisted (or before SMS cancellation/deletion finishes); in a serverless request this work may be terminated after the response. That leaves the cron with no marker to act on and permits the queued reminder to send. Collect and await these promises, and propagate or otherwise reliably record failures.
